17th axis · User-directed · Public-record only · Primary sources cited

First-degree family (spouses, parents, siblings, adult children) of flagged Canadian federal decision-makers, where their publicly documented financial, consulting, lobbying, board-appointment, or judicial activity overlaps with the decision-maker's federal role.

Each of the overlaps above has been individually reviewed under existing Canadian federal accountability mechanisms: Commissioner of Lobbying for lobbying, Ethics Commissioner for conflicts of interest, Canadian Judicial Council for judicial conduct, Canada Gazette for appointments, Elections Canada for contributions.

But the pattern formed by combining each flagged decision-maker with their spouse or family member's documented overlap is not the jurisdiction of any single oversight body. The Commissioner of Lobbying reviews the WE Charity lobbying registrations individually; the Ethics Commissioner reviewed Trudeau's breach individually; neither has scope to review the pattern itself .

This extends the central structural finding documented on the State of Investigation page: the Canadian federal accountability system distributes responsibility across independent oversight bodies so thoroughly that no body has jurisdiction over cross-axis or cross-relationship patterns . The 17th axis (this page) adds the spouse/family dimension to that finding.
